speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) how many cases of refusal of entry to the National Environment Agency’s (NEA) dengue inspection officers have been reported in the past three years; and (b) whether the Ministry has any plans to increase the penalties for individuals who refuse entry to NEA’s dengue inspection officers for inspection under the Control of Vectors and Pesticides Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for
text: the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment): Mr Speaker, most residents allow the National Environment Agency's (NEA) officers to inspect their premises after the officers have explained the need to conduct checks for mosquito breeding and stem dengue transmission.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for
text: In such instances, NEA would offer to reschedule the inspection to another time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for
text: Eventually, most of them will comply and facilitate our inspections.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for
text: Individuals who fail to comply with the notice can be charged under section 45 of CVPA for obstructing or hindering NEA officers from performing their duties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for
text: In light of the increasing number of dengue cases, I urge all individuals and premises managers to take urgent action to break the disease transmission by adopting good housekeeping habits to prevent mosquito breeding.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I note from the Senior Parliamentary Secretary's reply that the number of people who refused entry to NEA officers are relatively small.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is because, in my constituency, I have a large proportion of the elderly and, during my visits, I commonly hear from my elderly residents that they are very wary about opening their doors to strangers, even to those who seemingly wear uniforms because there are afraid of scams.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, my question is: how does NEA plan to create awareness of the role of the NEA inspection officers and to assuage elderly residents that these officers and their inspections are actually legitimate?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As mentioned in my reply, most of them do eventually allow access to their premises after engagement and explanation, and NEA has not had the right to take harsher action against them.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These residents also find that after they have allowed the officers to enter their premises, they also learned from the officers about potential breeding grounds for mosquitoes and how they could prevent such habitats from building up and invading their homes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, perhaps the Member can also help us to provide the number to his residents so that they can call by phone to check the authority card number against NEA records or, for those who can use the Internet, they can also check using the NEA website.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We could also look at, for example, in dengue cluster areas, perhaps putting up posters, with the support of local advisors, using their notice boards, to assure residents that NEA is doing the inspection to contain the spread of dengue and also how they may verify the identity of these officers.
